distinguishing_features: Adds a physical tuned-mass-damper hardware ring with shear springs at the nozzle flange to absorb resonant modal energy, rather than inferring damage from existing sensor signals
Changes the dynamic structural response (detuning natural frequency/damping) instead of derating the operating envelope or adjusting duty cycle
Targets the amplification of thermal-transient-driven dynamic stress at the nozzle root, not thermodynamic monitoring of EGT or strain
Predicts a measured stress-amplitude reduction verified by strain gauges, not a derived thermal-stress or efficiency indicator
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce resonant amplification of small thermal/flow transients into high cyclic stresses at the nozzle-to-shell junction without changing static pressure rating or material grade.
parsed.viable_reason: A tuned mass damper is a well-established, physically sound passive damping technique; the stated mass ratio and effective damping increase are plausible and the stress-reduction prediction is testable via strain gauges.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art uses structural dynamic modification (TMD detuning/damping) to address fatigue; all prior art relies on thermodynamic inference, envelope capping, or monitoring, so applying a TMD to a pressure-vessel nozzle to decouple resonant forcing is not an obvious step from that art.
